source: NCERT Class XII, Contemporary World Politics, Ch. 1 (The Cold War Era).

sections.heading: 1. What Was the Cold War?
points: The **Cold War** = the period of intense **rivalry and tension between the USA (and the Western bloc) and the USSR (and the Eastern bloc)** after **World War II (1945)** until the collapse of the USSR (1991).
It was a war of **ideology (capitalism vs communism), arms race, and influence** — but **not a direct 'hot' war** between the superpowers.
The world became **bipolar** (two power centres).

sections.heading: 2. Alliances and Crises
points: Military alliances: **NATO (Western, 1949)** and the **Warsaw Pact (Eastern, 1955)**.
Crises: the **Cuban Missile Crisis (1962)** (USA-USSR nuclear brink), the **Korean War, Vietnam War, Berlin blockade**.
**Deterrence** and the arms race (**MAD — Mutually Assured Destruction**) prevented direct war.

sections.heading: 3. Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
points: **Non-Alignment** — newly independent nations chose **not to join either bloc**.
Founders: **Nehru (India), Nasser (Egypt), Tito (Yugoslavia), Sukarno (Indonesia), Nkrumah (Ghana)**.
The **first NAM Summit was held at Belgrade (1961)**.
NAM advocated **peace, disarmament, decolonisation, and a fair world order (later NIEO)**.

sections.heading: 4. Significance and End
points: NAM gave newly independent countries a **voice and independence in foreign policy**.
The Cold War shaped global politics for over four decades.
It ended with the **disintegration of the USSR (1991)**, leaving the USA as the sole superpower.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Cold War = USA (West) vs USSR (East); bipolar world; 1945–1991.
Alliances: NATO (1949, West), Warsaw Pact (1955, East).
Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) = nuclear flashpoint; MAD = deterrence.
NAM founders: Nehru, Nasser, Tito, Sukarno, Nkrumah; first summit Belgrade (1961).
Cold War ended with the collapse of the USSR (1991).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **NATO (1949) = Western bloc; Warsaw Pact (1955) = Eastern bloc.**
The **first NAM summit was at Belgrade (1961)**.
The **Cuban Missile Crisis** was in **1962**.
Non-Alignment ≠ neutrality/isolation — it meant an **independent** foreign policy.
